events.author: Velociryx
events.name: A Matter of Faith

options.text: We don't mind them visiting, but the longer they stay, the more likely they are to try and spread their faith.
Allow them to remain, but have local leaders highlight the cultural aspects of their so-called Religion and take steps to minimize the spread of the tenets of their faith.
Instruct local leaders to divert civic resources to make them feel welcome.

events.text: During the now completed festival in the city of [city], practitioners of [religion] visited our great city and joined us in celebration. Well and good, but they seem inclined to linger. Do we want that?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: A Remarkable Discovery

options.text: I shall keep them for myself and study their wisdom.
These scrolls should be turned over to my scholars to see if they can use the knowledge they contain to further our current research.
We should create a traveling display so that they can be shared within our realm.

events.text: Your recent hunt was something special. Not only did you manage to secure badly needed food for your people, but your scouts also discovered a hidden cave. At one point in the distant past, some unknown civilization used this as a repository for knowledge. Hundreds of scrolls were discovered, along with idols paying homage to long forgotten gods, an impressive treasure trove indeed that could unlock important secrets. The question then, is what to do with them?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Achievement

options.text: Achievement.

events.text: Achievement

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Adult Children

options.text: [character] did all the hard work on the hunt.
[character] struck the final blow, and thus deserves the credit.
We can settle this dispute equitably by hanging the trophy in the royal palace.

events.text: Your adult children [character] and [character] recently attended a royal hunt, on which [character] spotted and stalked an exquisite fourteen-point stag. At the last moment, [character] cut in and shot the beast himself, even having the gall to claim ownership over the trophy! The squabbling siblings confront you in the royal palace. Which of your children should be given ownership of the trophy, and the subsequent bragging rights?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Akam and Puram

options.text: Find the best works of Akam, reflective explorations of human emotion.
Listen to the Puram, epic tales of heroes, kingdoms and dynasties.

events.text: Across the years that the Sangam has been taking place, poets and orators have flooded into [city] to share their work with the collective. Now that it is complete, the judges report that there is a wide mix of different works, with most falling into the categories of internal and external, Akam and Puram.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Be Prepared

options.text: Diplomacy must be explored before all else.
Summon our best officers to explore a coming conflict.
We must restrain our emotions and use wise judgment.
I will send messengers across [rival] to recruit volunteers.

events.text: With tensions running high between [rival] and [rival], the court debates ways to approach diplomacy or perhaps... war. [character] speaks strongly in support of peaceful measures, while soldier [character] rages against the appearance of weakness. Passions reach a breaking point, as courtiers and advisors voice their differing opinions. How will you interject on our rifts with [rival]?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Blood and Sand

options.text: Formalize the Sand Pits by building a proper structure around the impromptu arena, turning it into a means to subtly control the population.
It's a simple curiosity that will die out in short order. On the other hand, [character] is a good find, and would make an excellent addition to your Court.
Enjoy the Sand Pits while they exist, and hone your skills in battle there.

events.text: One of the curious side effects of the recent festival you held in the city of [city] was the creation of the Sand Pits, an informal arena that almost seemed to spring up overnight, giving the martially inclined festivalgoers a place to test themselves against each other. Of interest, the Sand Pits have remained, even though the festival itself is now over, and you're not at all sure how you feel about that. On the one hand, it's something of an eyesore, which makes it a blight on your fair city. On the other though, it does serve an important function and it could even give you the means to spot rising talent. In fact, in recent days, you've been impressed by the prowess of [character], who has won the last several competitions, and demonstrated by exceptional skill and bravery. The question is: What do you want to do about them?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Celebration of Our Many Blessings

options.text: Boot them out. We do not wish them spreading their faith here.
Allow them to remain but instruct the city leaders to treat them as cultural curiosities, and nothing more, preventing them from spreading their faith.
Welcome them with open arms and allow them to actively practice and spread their faith.

events.text: During the recently completed festival in the city of [city], acolytes of [religion] entered the city and participated in our celebration. The question is what should we do with them now?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Enablers

options.text: I desire men and women of pleasure!
Wine, wine, and more wine!
Nothing they can offer is of interest to me.

events.text: A troupe of exotic performers stops in [city] to entertain the people. During a short visit to the palace, the dancers and poets offer other, more unique services to those who wish to indulge themselves... Do you dare enjoy the revels?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Foresight

options.text: Yes.
No.

events.text: The walls of [city] stand ready to repel any invaders... or do they? You take them in, again, with a more critical eye. Would they truly be enough, if the city were in dire straits?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Fresh Perspectives

options.text: Let us add [character] to our Court. Another Merchant is always useful.
We should bring [character] into the fold. He looks promising indeed.
Let's pay to add [character] to our ranks.
As tempting as these Courtiers are, we're just not in a position to do that.

events.text: The most recent festival held in [city] was a tremendous success. [character] even put in an appearance, and a number of rising stars from among the [tribe] attracted your attention. Given that you and the [tribe] are on reasonably good terms, [character] has agreed to part with one of his own courtiers, if you'd be willing to pay to relocate the one you want to bring into your fold. The opportunity to bring new blood and fresh perspectives to Court could pay substantial long-term dividends. What say you?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: From Festival to Powder Keg

options.text: Don't get involved. Allow the Captain of the Watch to carry out his sentence.
Intervene and ransom the children back to their parents.
Intervene and let the children go free to keep peace with the [tribe].

events.text: During the closing days of the Festival in [city], the Captain of the City Watch arrested and detained a trio of [tribe] children for petty thievery. This is not something that would normally warrant your attention, but when the parents attempted to get their children back, the situation escalated. Although no one was killed, blood was spilled, and now the situation has reached a boiling point with the Captain of the Watch threatening to execute the children to send a message to the [tribe]. While many of the citizens of [city] support this action, there are others who are horrified by the prospect, which is how you became aware of the issue. How do you want to handle this?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Imports Boom

options.text: Invest in developing new trade routes to far off lands.
Focus on bulk imports.

events.text: Luxury does not come cheap. Which is good news for the merchants of [city], as demand opens up new trade and opportunities.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: One For The Storybooks

options.text: ...asked [character] to join you.
...shared the spoils of your hunt with the [tribe].
...accepted the help of the [tribe] to kill more game.

events.text: Your recent hunt was a smashing success, not the least of which because you chanced to encounter [character] while in the wilds. You...

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Pocketed

options.text: Mere hearsay.
We must at least ensure a new governor takes the reins.

events.text: The treasuries of [city] lie mysteriously empty, and while no one has leveled an accusation, it is considered common knowledge the riches found their way into the pockets of [character].

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Procession of the Gods

options.text: Perform a ritual sacrifice to appease the gods' anger.
Instruct that the city be cleaned and the festival held again.
Appoint a governor to improve the city for next year's festival.

events.text: The festival in [city] sees the gods of [religion] paraded around the city, their statues carried through the streets with singing and dancing. This is a chance for the gods to inspect the lands and appreciate the city. [character] sends you a message after the festival. He found the streets dirty and run-down and is worried that the city was not up to the god's expectation.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Sacred Games

options.text: Offer 500 gold if he becomes the winner of the games.
Use pride for your nation to appeal to him.
Suggest that he tries cheating.
Ignore the games and use your time for ruling instead.

events.text: The priests of have declared that there will be sacred games performed in [city] after the funeral games of old. Greeks from across the nation are invited to compete, while family rivalry is already heating up. Backing the [family] contender, the young scion [character], the other members of your family ask you to motivate the athlete to avoid the shame of losing.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Snake Charmer

options.text: A life for a life. Bring me the head of [character].
Revenge is not enough. All the [tribe] must pay.

events.text: A caravan of [tribe] performers stop in [city] to entertain the crowds. You and [character] attend a show, hoping for a night away from the squabbles of the court. During a wondrous display of exotic creatures, an animal handler hurls a hissing black snake into your private gallery. The fanged serpent strikes [character] before it is slashed to pieces. "Vengeance belongs to [character]!" shouts the handler, committing suicide before she can be caught.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Beautiful Festival

options.text: Relax and enjoy yourself to the full.
Smash a votive as a sign of your dedication to the gods.
Make offerings for physical health and wellbeing.
Make your excuses and avoid attending.

events.text: The people of [city] are hosting a grand festival in praise of Amun. The statue of the god is carried around the city streets on an ark as the people celebrate and the priests listen to petitioners. As a celebration of life and the community, you are asked to attend. How will you spend your time at the Beautiful Festival?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: The Fair

options.text: Let us add [character] to our collection of Courtiers.
We should bring [character] into the fold.
Forget the people, let's acquire those spices!
This is a wondrous offer, but it's just not something we can afford to take advantage of right now.

events.text: An odd thing happened at the conclusion of the festival in the city of [city]. Your people, and those who attended from neighboring lands did not want the good times to end, and for more than a week after you formally brought the city-wide celebration to a close, street vendors remained, and the entire city continued to maintain a festive atmosphere. During that time, you had the opportunity to wander the streets, disguised of course, so as not to draw undue attention, and you got the opportunity to meet many of your people in person, and see what foreigners truly thought about your fair city. The people of [tribe] impressed you, particularly [character], a skilled mercenary, and [character], a merchant of some renown. After speaking with [character] about the matter, you have convinced him to agree to allow one of them to enter your service, if you would be willing to compensate the tribe for their loss. [character] also mentions something else. He has recently come into possession of a supply of exotic spices. He would be willing to part with them if you'd be interested. You may have your pick of any of the three. What say you?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: The Grand Hunt

options.text: ...giving your generals the opportunity to hone their tactics.
...demonstrating that great things are possible.
...giving you a much needed break from the day to day rigors of ruling, which allowed you to view your Realm through fresh eyes.

events.text: People are still talking about the last Great Hunt you held. It was a smashing success that truly inspired your People by…

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Greatest of Poets

options.text: Insist that he joins your court.
Commission a great work of your deeds and lineage.
Ask to study under the great poet.

events.text: Out of the hundreds of poems that have been collected across the Sangam in [city], one out of ten have been composed by a single person. This poet, [character], has work capturing everything from the intimacies of love to the epics of heroes at war.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Legendary Sangams

options.text: Well, it was rather spectacular.
Build a literary academy to continue this work.

events.text: It is done. The great gathering of poets is over and the work is already disseminating through [rival], bringing in a new age of culture. Outside of the poetic works that have been collected, legends and tales are also building around the nature of the gathering itself, with some saying that each Sangam lasts for thousands of years.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Man of Reeds

options.text: End the festivities with a speech praising the city's hospitality.
End the festivities with a speech praising the revered hero.

events.text: The people of [city] have invited you to attend a celebration of their local cult. The Reed Man is said to have saved the city many years ago, and the streets fill with people asking for protection in the years to come. The actual worship takes place at night, as a young buck is slaughtered over a low altar where the blood flows across the sacred ground, said to be the tomb of this ancient hero.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: The Sword In The Stone

options.text: Perhaps we'll come up with a way to remove it later. For now, I shall keep it in my private collection.
Let us put it on display in the capital and allow its myth and mystery to grow.

events.text: During your recent hunt, your party made an unexpected discovery: a large rock formation with a sword embedded in it. Some effort was made to remove it on the spot, but when this proved impossible, you marked the spot on your map and vowed to send a party back for it later. That party has returned, but as yet, no one has been able to remove the sword from the stone. What will you do with the curiosity?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: The Traveling Circus

options.text: Send a heartfelt note of thanks to [character], expressing our appreciation for making our Festival all the brighter.
Ask them to remain for an extended engagement.
Hire [character], leader of the Traveling Circus. We know talent when we see it!
While the Festival was lovely, we lack the resources at the moment to take advantage of the other opportunities the traveling circus represents.

events.text: The recently concluded Festival in the city of [city] drew the attention of a traveling circus from the land of the [tribe]. A modest band of wagons led by [character] and filled with trade goods, games of chance and a few luxury items not normally found in [city], their presence was a wonderful addition to the festivities. In fact, it occurs to you that there might be an additional opportunity here...

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: The Zoological Society

options.text: Let us create a lush park and zoo, allowing our citizens to view and learn about them.
We should build enclosures that allow our wise men to study them. Surely there is much we could learn.
It's a wonderful idea, but not an expense we can currently afford.

events.text: The city of [city] is now home to a growing collection of strange and wonderful animals from faraway lands. It occurs to you that you could put these fascinating creatures to good, productive use by rounding them up and creating a centralized location to house them in. A couple of enticing options come to mind once that is done. It all depends on what direction you'd like to take things.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Time to Celebrate

options.text: The oldest and most deserving.
The head of every noble family.
The poorest of the poor.

events.text: The people are happy, and the change of season is nigh. It is time to celebrate! The [family] and [family] families have volunteered to fund a festival in honor of those who have given so much to the nation. They ask for our wisdom about whom to raise up at this event.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Toward a Glorious Future

options.text: Excite the populace of [city] to even greater civic activism.
Tell the history of our people in pictures carved onto our newly built walls so that all may know of our works and deeds.
Encourage learned men to [city], secure in the knowledge they may study here in peace and safety.

events.text: The newly completed walls around [city] are thick and imposing. Once completed, your people feel safe and secure in your care and know they are in capable hands. You are wise enough not to waste the goodwill your newly crafted defenses have created. The only question is, how best to channel it?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Translations

options.text: Begin the translations now. Knowledge is worth it.
Ignorance is bliss. The people can be controlled better that way.
I will translate them myself, and I will be sure that it bolsters my image.

events.text: The [family] family come asking if you can spare your scribes to translate some foreign text that the family has acquired into our own tongue. They say that it could expose important knowledge from the wider world.
